title: the store-rebuild rung refuses a real v2 migration with a raw SQLite constraint that names neither thread nor id, and its remedy sends the operator to a doctor that can only tell them to re-run the command that just failed
body:
**Driven on the shipped pair (`intent` and `intentd` both `da5919e8fce833bec04d03e8f92fc554223d078c`, `git rev-list --count da5919e8f..HEAD -- native/rust surface` = 0) against `Lamplight` at its pinned pre-migration revision `fe5dff3e6f9259c3fde0c4e696c9241db31d0617` -- 12,282 files, 156 `acceptance.md`, zero canon, a genuine unmigrated 2.19.0 estate extracted by `git archive` into a scratch tree.** Not a fixture.

## THE MIGRATOR HAS TWO REFUSAL RUNGS AND ONLY ONE OF THEM CAN BE ACTED ON

**Phase A (residue) is exemplary and this issue is not about it.** It refuses with a per-line classed report -- `intent/st/ST0201/acceptance.md:59 -- unread-field -- AC-05.3 carries \`on\`, which this grammar does not read` -- a remedy per finding, and a joined summary (`refused 8 finding(s) -- unread-field: 8`). It is atomic in the strong sense: tree byte-identical AND **no `intent/.cache/` is created at all**. I acted on all 8 findings mechanically, exactly as the remedies instruct, and Phase A then passed.

**The store-rebuild rung, one rung further in, leaks its driver's error:**

```
error: could not update the runtime store
  caused by: sqlite: UNIQUE constraint failed: tests.thread_id, tests.id
  caused by: UNIQUE constraint failed: tests.thread_id, tests.id
  caused by: Error code 1555: A PRIMARY KEY constraint failed
  remedy: the change was not made. Do NOT delete the store -- it is the source of truth, not a cache, and the committed extract may be older than it. Run `intent doctor` to inspect the estate
```

**It names neither the thread nor the id.** The estate contains exactly two offenders -- `ST0298` `AT-02.3` and `ST0198` `AT-16.1`, both under `intent/st/COMPLETED/` -- and Lamplight's real migration commit `4ffd0fe1f` says `two duplicate AT ids demoted`, so this is the defect that was hit for real and fixed by hand. **A one-command scan finds them, but only once you already know what you are looking for**, and nothing in the output tells you that.

## AND THE REMEDY IT PRINTS CLOSES A LOOP WITH NO EXIT

`intent doctor`, on this same estate, in full:

```
residue: intent/.config/config.json -- unmigrated -- this project has not been migrated to Intent v3 -- it declares Intent 2.19.0, and 353 steel threads carry v2 canon this binary cannot read (ST0001, ST0002, ST0003, and 350 more) -- run `intent upgrade` to migrate this project to Intent v3
  remedy: migrate the project first -- every other finding on it is downstream of this one
doctor: 1 finding(s) across 0 thread(s), 0 issue(s), 0 view(s), 0 file(s)
```

**It names zero duplicates, zero AT rows, and sends the operator back to `intent upgrade` -- the command that just failed and referred them here.** `doctor` reads the model, the model is empty because the migration is what would fill it, so on an unmigrated estate `doctor` can only ever say the one thing it said. The referral is not weak; it is structurally incapable of answering.

## THE SAME MESSAGE IS WRITTEN FOR A PROJECT THIS ONE IS NOT

`Do NOT delete the store -- it is the source of truth, not a cache, and the committed extract may be older than it` is correct and important **on a live v3 project**. Here it is printed on a project that has never had a store, about `intent/.cache/intent.db` -- a **0-row, schema-only file created seconds earlier by the failure itself** (`threads`, `tests`, `criteria`, `issues` all count 0; tables present). Every clause misfires: it is in a directory named `.cache`, there is no committed extract for it to be newer than, and the operator is being warned off deleting an artefact of the very failure they are reading about.

## WHAT IS NOT BROKEN, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

**The rollback is honest.** Zero rows land, the tracked tree is byte-identical, the re-run fails identically and deterministically with the leftover store present, and nothing is corrupted. `Facade::upgrade`'s `applied.rollback()` arm does its job on a 12k-file estate. **The refusal is inert; it is the reporting that strands you.**

## THE CLASS, WHICH IS THE REUSABLE PART

**All three symptoms are one defect: a correct message printed for a different situation.** The sqlite text is correct for someone reading a database; the store warning is correct for a v3 operator; the `doctor` referral is correct on a migrated project. Each is right somewhere and none is right here, and **nothing in the output distinguishes the two cases**, which is exactly why it reads as helpful while leading nowhere. The fix is at the rung, not in the strings: the store-rebuild failure should name the artefact and the id the way Phase A already does, and should not refer to a reader that cannot see the model it is complaining about.

## SUGGESTED SHAPE, NOT A DESIGN

Phase A already proves the estate can be reported on before the model exists. The duplicate-id check belongs there, next to `unread-field`, where it can say the file, the line, the thread and the id -- and where the existing atomicity guarantee already holds. That is a relocation of a check, not a new instrument.

## HONEST NOTE ON MY OWN INSTRUMENT

**My first duplicate scan globbed `intent/st/*/acceptance.md` and returned "no duplicates" -- 13 files of 156.** v2 expresses status as a directory, so the offenders sat in `COMPLETED/` where the glob could not reach. **The positive control passed** -- 320 AT rows matched -- **because it tested the PATTERN and not the POPULATION**, which is the same shape as a pattern-vs-subject miss earlier the same day. The finding above stands on the corrected 156-file scan, and the tool's own error is what told me my scan was wrong.
